fplAddHI.note: 2026, Hawaii, added for each extra person

snapGrossPct.note: gross income test, % of poverty, Oct 2026 to Sep 2027

mealsReducedPct.note: reduced-price meals, % of poverty, July 2026 to June 2027 (free meals at 130%)

chipMaxPct.note: highest state limit for children (New York), January 2026; the median state is 255%

mspIncomeYearCouple.note: 2026 QI limit $2,455 a month, married couple

ssiIncomeYear.note: screening estimate: 2026 federal payment $994 a month x 12, single

ssiIncomeYearCouple.note: screening estimate: 2026 federal payment $1,491 a month x 12, couple

eitcIncomeKids.note: tax year 2025, 3 or more children, single or head of household

eitcIncomeKidsJoint.note: tax year 2025, 3 or more children, married filing jointly

eitcIncomeNoKidsJoint.note: tax year 2025, no children, married filing jointly

ctcIncome.note: full credit up to this income, single

ctcIncomeJoint.note: full credit up to this income, filing jointly

freeFileIncome.note: IRS Free File guided software, AGI limit

liheapPct.note: federal maximum is the greater of 150% of poverty or 60% of state median income

tanfScreenPct.note: screening estimate: each state sets its own limit, usually lower

rentScreenPct.note: screening estimate: HUD limits are 50% and 80% of area median income, which vary by area

healthCenterPct.note: about 90% of health center patients have incomes under 200% of poverty

vaPensionIncome.note: MAPR, veteran with no dependents, from 1 Dec 2025

schemes.name: SNAP (food stamps)
schemes.gives: Money each month on an EBT card to spend on food. Up to $306 a month for one person, or $808 for three.
schemes.how: Apply to your state's SNAP office, online, by phone or in person.

rule.expr: income at or under 130% of the poverty line (gross income test)
rule.txt: Income under 130% of the poverty line
rule.fail: Income over 130% of the poverty line

schemes.name: Medicaid
schemes.gives: Free or very low-cost health cover for you or your children, including doctor visits, hospital care and prescriptions.
schemes.how: Apply through HealthCare.gov or straight to your state Medicaid office, any time of year.
schemes.timing: From January 2027, adults covered on income alone may need to meet a monthly work rule.

rule.expr: income at or under 138% of the poverty line in an expansion state, or pregnant or with children at that income, or gets SSI
rule.txt: Income under your state's Medicaid line
rule.fail: Your state covers few adults on income alone, but children, pregnancy and disability can still qualify

schemes.name: Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
schemes.gives: A monthly payment if you're 65 or over, blind or disabled, with little income or savings. Up to $994 a month, or $1,491 for a couple.
schemes.how: Apply online or call Social Security to book an appointment.

rule.expr: aged 65 or over, or has a disability
rule.txt: Aged 65 or over, or has a health condition

rule.expr: yearly income under $11,928, or $17,892 for a couple
rule.txt: Income under the SSI payment level
rule.fail: Income likely above the SSI payment level

rule.expr: savings $2,000 or less, or $3,000 for a couple
rule.txt: Savings $2,000 or less ($3,000 for a couple)

schemes.name: WIC
schemes.gives: Healthy food and nutrition help while you're pregnant, after birth, and for children under 5.
schemes.how: Contact your local WIC clinic to book an appointment. If you get SNAP or Medicaid, bring proof and you can skip the income check.

rule.expr: pregnant, or has a child under 5
rule.txt: Pregnant or has a child under 5

rule.expr: income at or under 185% of the poverty line, or gets SNAP or Medicaid
rule.txt: Income under 185% of the poverty line, or gets SNAP or Medicaid
rule.fail: Income over 185% of the poverty line

schemes.name: Free and reduced-price school meals
schemes.gives: Free school lunch and breakfast if your income is under 130% of the poverty line, or meals at a reduced price under 185%.
schemes.how: Ask your child's school for a meal application. If you get SNAP, your children are usually signed up without one.

rule.expr: has a child under 19
rule.txt: Has a child under 19

rule.expr: income at or under 185% of the poverty line, or gets SNAP
rule.txt: Income under 185% of the poverty line, or gets SNAP
rule.fail: Income over 185% of the poverty line

schemes.name: Head Start
schemes.gives: Free early learning for children from birth to age 5.
schemes.how: Contact a Head Start program near you. Children in families who get TANF or SSI, or who are homeless or in foster care, can join whatever the income.

rule.expr: has a child under 5
rule.txt: Has a child under 5

rule.expr: income under the poverty line, or gets SSI
rule.txt: Income under the poverty line, or gets SSI

schemes.name: Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP)
schemes.gives: Low-cost health cover for children, and in some states pregnant women, when your income is too high for Medicaid. You won't pay more than 5% of your income a year.
schemes.how: Apply any time of year through HealthCare.gov or your state. Cover can start straight away.
schemes.worthChecking: Each state sets its own income limit, so your state decides

rule.expr: has a child under 19
rule.txt: Has a child under 19

rule.expr: income at or under 405% of the poverty line (the highest state limit)
rule.txt: Income within the range states cover
rule.fail: Income above every state's CHIP limit

schemes.name: Marketplace premium tax credit
schemes.gives: Money off the monthly cost of a health plan you buy through the Marketplace.
schemes.how: Apply at HealthCare.gov or your state's Marketplace, using your best estimate of this year's income.
schemes.timing: Enroll by December 15 for cover from January 1.
schemes.worthChecking: Depends on plan prices where you live and whether a job offers you health cover

rule.expr: income between 100% and 400% of the poverty line, and above the Medicaid line where Medicaid is expanded
rule.txt: Income between 100% and 400% of the poverty line
rule.fail: Income outside the 100% to 400% range, or Medicaid covers you instead

rule.expr: under 65
rule.txt: Under 65
rule.fail: Aged 65 or over: Medicare is the usual cover

rule.expr: doesn't get Medicaid
rule.txt: Doesn't get Medicaid

schemes.name: Medicare Savings Program
schemes.gives: Your state pays your Medicare Part B premium, and at the lowest incomes your deductibles and copays too. It also gives you Extra Help with drug costs.
schemes.how: Apply to your state Medicaid office. Some states accept you even above these limits, so apply if you're close.

rule.expr: aged 65 or over
rule.txt: Aged 65 or over

rule.expr: yearly income $21,792 or less, or $29,460 for a couple
rule.txt: Income under the Medicare Savings Program limit
rule.fail: Income over the Medicare Savings Program limit

rule.expr: savings $9,950 or less, or $14,910 for a couple
rule.txt: Savings $9,950 or less ($14,910 for a couple)

schemes.name: Extra Help with Medicare drug costs
schemes.gives: Help paying for Medicare Part D: no premium or deductible, and low fixed prices for each prescription.
schemes.how: Apply online or by phone with Social Security. You get it without applying if you have full Medicaid, SSI or a Medicare Savings Program.

rule.expr: aged 65 or over
rule.txt: Aged 65 or over

rule.expr: yearly income $23,940 or less, or $32,460 for a couple
rule.txt: Income under the Extra Help limit
rule.fail: Income over the Extra Help limit

rule.expr: savings $18,090 or less, or $36,100 for a couple
rule.txt: Savings $18,090 or less ($36,100 for a couple)

schemes.name: Community health centers
schemes.gives: Medical, dental and mental health care with fees based on your income. They see everyone, even if you can't pay.
schemes.how: Find a health center near you and call to book. Tell them your income and household size so they can lower your fee.

rule.expr: income at or under 200% of the poverty line
rule.txt: Income under 200% of the poverty line
rule.fail: Income over 200% of the poverty line

schemes.name: Lifeline phone and internet discount
schemes.gives: Up to $9.25 off your phone or internet bill each month, or up to $34.25 on Tribal lands.
schemes.how: Check and apply on the Lifeline website, then choose a phone or internet company that offers Lifeline.

rule.expr: income at or under 135% of the poverty line, or gets SNAP, Medicaid or SSI
rule.txt: Income under 135% of the poverty line, or gets SNAP, Medicaid or SSI
rule.fail: Income over 135% of the poverty line

schemes.name: LIHEAP energy bill help
schemes.gives: Help paying your home energy bills.
schemes.how: Contact your state or local LIHEAP office. Some take applications online; others ask you to come in.
schemes.worthChecking: Your state sets its own limit and funding can run out, so apply early

rule.expr: income at or under 150% of the poverty line, or gets SNAP or SSI
rule.txt: Income under 150% of the poverty line, or gets SNAP or SSI
rule.fail: Income over 150% of the poverty line, though some states go higher

schemes.name: Weatherization Assistance Program
schemes.gives: Home improvements that lower your energy costs, paid for by the program.
schemes.how: Contact your state weatherization office to find your local provider and apply.
schemes.worthChecking: Your local provider checks your home, and there can be a wait

rule.expr: income at or under 200% of the poverty line, or gets SSI
rule.txt: Income under 200% of the poverty line, or gets SSI
rule.fail: Income over 200% of the poverty line

schemes.name: TANF cash assistance
schemes.gives: Cash help for families with children to pay for food, housing, energy and child care, plus help with job training.
schemes.how: Apply to the TANF office in the state where you live. It may have a different name in your state.
schemes.worthChecking: Each state sets its own rules and income limit, often well under the poverty line

rule.expr: has a child under 18 or is pregnant
rule.txt: Has a child under 18 or is pregnant

rule.expr: income at or under 100% of the poverty line
rule.txt: Income under 100% of the poverty line
rule.fail: Income over 100% of the poverty line

schemes.name: Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8)
schemes.gives: Help paying your rent, through a voucher from your local housing agency.
schemes.how: Apply to your local public housing agency. Waiting lists are long, so it helps to apply to several agencies.
schemes.worthChecking: Limits depend on your area's median income, and waiting lists can be long or closed

rule.expr: rents privately or lives with family or friends
rule.txt: Rents or lives with others
rule.fail: Already in public housing or owns the home

rule.expr: income at or under 200% of the poverty line (screening estimate)
rule.txt: Income under 200% of the poverty line
rule.fail: Income over 200% of the poverty line

schemes.name: Public housing
schemes.gives: A home rented from your local housing agency, for people on low incomes.
schemes.how: Contact your local housing agency. If you're accepted, you join a waiting list until a home is free.
schemes.worthChecking: Limits depend on your area's median income, and waiting lists can be long or closed

rule.expr: rents privately or lives with family or friends
rule.txt: Rents or lives with others
rule.fail: Already in public housing or owns the home

rule.expr: income at or under 200% of the poverty line (screening estimate)
rule.txt: Income under 200% of the poverty line
rule.fail: Income over 200% of the poverty line

schemes.name: Earned Income Tax Credit
schemes.gives: A tax credit for people who work on a low or moderate income, worth up to $8,231 with three or more children.
schemes.how: Claim it on your federal tax return. Free filing help can do this for you.

rule.expr: works or is self-employed
rule.txt: Has earned income

rule.expr: income under the EITC limit for the family (with children up to $61,555, or $68,675 filing jointly; without children aged 25 to 64 and up to $19,104, or $26,214 jointly)
rule.txt: Income under the EITC limit

schemes.name: Child Tax Credit
schemes.gives: Up to $2,200 off your tax for each child under 17. If you owe little tax, up to $1,700 per child can come back as a refund.
schemes.how: Claim it on your federal tax return. You and each child need a Social Security number.

rule.expr: has a child under 17
rule.txt: Has a child under 17

rule.expr: income $200,000 or less, or $400,000 filing jointly
rule.txt: Income under $200,000 ($400,000 jointly)
rule.fail: Income over the full credit limit

schemes.name: Free tax filing help
schemes.gives: File your federal return for free: IRS Free File software if your income is $95,000 or less, or free help from IRS-certified volunteers (VITA) if you earn about $70,244 or less.
schemes.how: Use IRS Free File online, or find a free VITA or TCE site near you. Never pay to claim credits you can claim for free.
schemes.timing: IRS Free File opens again in January 2027.

rule.expr: income $95,000 or less
rule.txt: Income $95,000 or less
rule.fail: Income over the Free File limit

schemes.name: Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI)
schemes.gives: Monthly payments if a condition stops you working for a year or more and you've paid into Social Security.
schemes.how: Apply online or call Social Security. Generally you need 40 work credits, 20 of them in the last 10 years.
schemes.worthChecking: Depends on your work record and Social Security's medical decision

rule.expr: not working, or off sick
rule.txt: Not working or off sick

rule.expr: has a health condition that makes daily life hard
rule.txt: Health condition affects daily life
rule.fail: No health condition affecting daily life

schemes.name: Social Security survivors benefits
schemes.gives: Monthly payments if your husband or wife has died, from age 60 (50 if you're disabled) or at any age if you care for their child under 16. There's also a one-time $255 payment.
schemes.how: Call Social Security to apply. You can't apply online.
schemes.worthChecking: Depends on your age and your partner's work record

rule.expr: husband, wife or partner died
rule.txt: Lost a husband, wife or partner

schemes.name: Unemployment insurance
schemes.gives: Weekly payments while you look for work, if you lost your job through no fault of your own.
schemes.how: File with the state where you worked, ideally the week you lose your job.
schemes.worthChecking: Your state checks why the job ended and what you earned in the last year or two

rule.expr: not working
rule.txt: Not working

schemes.name: Federal Pell Grant
schemes.gives: A grant for college that you don't have to pay back, up to $7,395 a year.
schemes.how: Fill in the FAFSA form for the year you plan to study. Your college works out the amount.
schemes.worthChecking: Only if you're going to college, or plan to

rule.expr: aged 17 or over
rule.txt: Aged 17 or over

schemes.name: VA health care
schemes.gives: Health care for veterans through VA.
schemes.how: Apply online or call the VA health care hotline, weekdays 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. ET.
schemes.worthChecking: VA checks your service length and discharge

rule.expr: served in the US military
rule.txt: Served in the military

schemes.name: Veterans Pension
schemes.gives: A monthly payment for wartime veterans on a low income who are 65 or over or disabled. Up to $17,441 a year for a veteran on their own.
schemes.how: Apply online with VA, or get help from an accredited representative.
schemes.worthChecking: Needs wartime service, and VA counts your whole net worth

rule.expr: served in the US military
rule.txt: Served in the military

rule.expr: aged 65 or over, or has a disability, or gets SSI
rule.txt: Aged 65 or over, or disabled

rule.expr: yearly income under $17,441
rule.txt: Income under the pension rate

rule.expr: savings $163,699 or less
rule.txt: Savings under the net worth limit
rule.fail: Savings over the net worth limit

schemes.name: VA disability compensation
schemes.gives: A monthly payment if an illness or injury was caused or made worse by your military service.
schemes.how: File a claim online, by mail, in person or through an accredited representative.
schemes.worthChecking: VA decides whether your condition is linked to your service

rule.expr: served in the US military
rule.txt: Served in the military

rule.expr: has a health condition that makes daily life hard
rule.txt: Health condition affects daily life
rule.fail: No health condition affecting daily life

schemes.name: Unclaimed money
schemes.gives: Money owed to you that's been handed to the state. Old savings bonds, FHA mortgage refunds and lost pensions can be found too.
schemes.how: Search free with your state's unclaimed property office, and every state you've lived in. Never pay a finder company.

rule.expr: lives in the US
rule.txt: Lives in the US

clashes.text: If Medicaid covers you, you can't also get Marketplace savings, so apply for Medicaid first.
A Medicare Savings Program that pays your Part B premium gives you Extra Help without a separate application.
Both are claimed on the same tax return, and free filing help can claim them for you.
With SNAP, your children usually get free school meals without filling in a form.
SNAP and WIC can be used together, and SNAP means you skip WIC's income check.
